Definition: past participle of a compound of G575 and G1096; absent, i.e. deceased (figuratively, renounced):--being dead.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in the verse that carries the cross. Christ bare our sins in His own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness — the word is the participle for having died to something, being gone from it altogether.
TheologicalSignificance: To be dead to sins is not to be numb to them; it is to have left them behind the way a dead man leaves a house.
